text:
alex: Heads-up — after the canary this morning we started seeing a jump in un-attributed tokens in the quota dashboard. seems like routing policy headers are getting dropped :confused:

rachel: I noticed alerts too, support is getting a couple tickets asking why quota shows 'unknown' tenant.

jamie: can you paste a sample request header from the canary?

alex: sure — simplified curl from the canary hosts:
```http
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Route-Policy: tenant=acme;quota_group=10
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.12
```
console still shows route_policy=null for those tokens.

mike: deploy-bot shows the canary rolled to proxy pool proxy-v2 (3 hosts) at 08:12 UTC.

eng-bot: deploy status: canary success on proxy-v2 (3/3), no host-level errors reported.

jamie: quick hypothesis: the internal proxy does h2 multiplexing for long-lived connections and we had a change that normalizes unknown headers -> dropped when reusing streams. saw something similar with tracing headers before.

rachel: that aligns with support timeline — spike started ~08:13.

sara: can we repro locally? jamie, any suggested repro steps?

jamie: easiest repro is to run a tiny node script with http2 + keepAlive and send X-Route-Policy repeatedly, inspect what proxy forwards. will post snippet in a sec.

alex: here's a quick curl loop that shows mismatch when using HTTP/2 multiplexed proxy vs plain HTTP/1.1
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do
  curl -k -H "X-Route-Policy: tenant=acme;quota_group=10" \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -X POST https://proxy-v2.internal/v1/generate -d '{}' >/dev/null &
done
```
then check proxy logs, we saw ~30% lacked the header.

mike: urgent question — do we rollback the proxy canary? customers impacted?

rachel: support reported 2 paying customers affected (quota show as external), finance alerted. i'd prefer rollback until fix unless we can hotfix quickly.

jamie: quick mitigation: proxy config can map fallback header X-Proxy-Route -> X-Route-Policy if present, while we root-cause. that requires a config push but is fast. alternative is to ship SDK change to duplicate header under a safe name (X-Route-Policy-B) — but SDK release is slower.

alex: can we also add telemetry to Console so we can see "header_received" boolean per request (sampled) — that will help confirm fix.

sara: i'll take telemetry tile change. small change: add a sampled boolean and a new chart for header presence over time. low-risk.

mike: i'll coordinate rollback if needed. what's the timeline for proxy fallback mapping?

jamie: if we approve, i can push mapping in 15-30m and monitor. it's a config change only.

rachel: +1 to config mapping for now. mike, hold rollback until mapping is in and we observe.

eng-bot: config push queued: proxy-v2 fallback-header-map (X-Proxy-Route -> X-Route-Policy) by jamie. dry-run in 2m.

alex: after mapping applied, observed header presence returned to ~99% and quota attribution looks normal.

rachel: thanks team. next steps?

jamie: follow-ups: 1) postmortem on why proxy dropped headers on h2 reuse (owner: jamie) 2) SDKs should implement a duplicated header fallback to ensure clients behind weird networking keep attribution (owners: alex for python, mike for node/ts, sara for go) 3) console telemetry tile (owner: sara) 4) add integration tests hitting proxy with h2 keepalive (owner: eng-platform team)

alex: i'll open short-lived issues and link to this thread. plan to ship SDK duplicates as opt-in flag first to avoid breaking proxies that choke on unknown headers.

mike: noted. i'll prepare node/ts PR and a canary plan. will avoid a breaking release — opt-in flag + env var.

rachel: update support and finance with timeline and that we mitigated without rollback. i'll draft the customer note.

ops-bot: created incident INC-2026-0423 for quota-attribution spike, tie to PRs and config change.

alex: thanks all — great quick triage. archive thread after owners acked on the corresponding issues. :thumbsup:
